result.topic_en: Notes on a hypothetical prime-number machine and the limits of what it can prove, a struck-out remark on successive osculating circles of a curve, deciding primality in finite time, and a remark praising Weierstrass as the Euclid of analysis.

items.quote:
Wie kann man eine Primzahlmaschine construiren, welche
bei beständiger Heizung immer mehr Primzahlen liefert.
items.english: How can one construct a prime-number machine which, with continuous heating, delivers more and more primes?

items.quote:
Mit einer solchen Maschine lässt sich nicht der Nachweis
von unendlich viele Primzahlen führen!
items.english: With such a machine one cannot carry out the proof that there are infinitely many primes!

items.quote:
Die aufeinanderfolgenden Krümmungskreise einer
Kurve schneiden sich nicht, weil die Entfernung ihrer
Mittelpunkte (die Sehne der Evolute) kleiner ist als
die Differenz ihrer Radien (der Bogen der Evolute)
items.english: Successive osculating circles of a curve do not intersect, because the distance between their centres (the chord of the evolute) is smaller than the difference of their radii (the arc of the evolute).

items.english: If an arbitrarily large but definite (number/prime) is given, a way can always be found by which we can decide in a definite finite time, e.g. a human lifetime, whether it is a prime or not.
